1. Noun এর post modifier হিসেবে- (subject + verb + noun + adjective clause).
2. Subject এর post modifier হিসেবে- (Subject + adjective clause + verb + object).

Parts of a Paragraph: 

A standard academic or structured paragraph consists of 3 main parts:

1. Topic Sentence
- A sentence that expresses the main idea of a paragraph is called Topic Sentence.
- It is the opening sentence of a paragraph.
- It introduces the main idea or central theme of the paragraph.

2. Supporting Sentences (Body)
- These sentences develop, explain, and support the main idea of the paragraph.
- They may include details, facts, examples, reasons, or explanations.

3. Concluding Sentence
- It is the final sentence of the paragraph.
- It summarizes the main point or restates the topic sentence in different words.
- It may also provide a smooth transition to the next paragraph.

Parts of a Letter

Whether formal or informal, a standard letter contains 6 key parts:

1. Heading (Sender's Address & Date)
- Placed at the top of the letter.
- It includes the sender's contact details and the date on which the letter is written.

2. Inside Address (Recipient's Address) (Formal letters only)
- It includes the name, title, and address of the person receiving the letter.

3. Salutation (Greeting)
- It is the opening greeting of the letter.
- Examples: Dear Mr. Smith, / Dear Friend,

4. Body of the Letter
- It contains the core message of the letter and is generally divided into three sections:

• Opening: Purpose of writing.
• Main Content: Explanation and details.
• Closing: Expected action or final thoughts.

5. Complimentary Close
- It is the polite sign-off used at the end of the letter.
- Examples: Sincerely, Yours faithfully, Best regards, etc.

6. Signature & Typed Name
- It includes the sender's handwritten signature followed by their full printed name and designation, if applicable.

Parts of a Formal Application (Job / Leave / Official Request)

A formal application or cover letter generally follows a standardized layout and consists of 7–8 key parts:

1. Header (Sender's Information & Date)
- It includes the sender's name, address, contact number, email address, and date.

2. Inside Address (Designation & Receiver's Office)
- It contains the designation and official address of the receiver.
- Examples: To The Principal, The Hiring Manager, The Managing Director, etc.

3. Subject Line
- It is a concise line that clearly states the exact purpose of the application.
- Examples: Subject: Application for leave of absence / Subject: Application for the post of English Lecturer.

4. Salutation
- It is the formal greeting used to address the receiver.
- Examples: Respected Sir/Madam, / Dear Hiring Manager,

5. Body of the Application
- It contains the main message of the application and is generally divided into three sections:

• Introduction: States the purpose of writing or the position being applied for.
• Body Paragraph: Provides relevant details such as qualifications, experience, or reasons for leave/request.
• Conclusion: Expresses hope for a positive response, consideration, or approval.

6. Complimentary Closing
- It is the formal sign-off used at the end of the application.
- Examples: Yours obediently, Yours sincerely, Sincerely yours, etc.

7. Signature Block
- It includes the applicant's signature and name.
- It may also include designation, roll/ID number, contact information, or other relevant details.

8. Enclosures / Attachments (Optional / If applicable)
- It contains a list of documents attached with the application.
- Examples: CV/Resume, Certificates, Medical Certificate, etc.

Parts of a Letter

Whether formal or informal, a standard letter contains 6 key parts:

1. Heading (Sender's Address & Date)
- Placed at the top of the letter.
- It includes the sender's contact details and the date on which the letter is written.

2. Inside Address (Recipient's Address) (Formal letters only)
- It includes the name, title, and address of the person receiving the letter.

3. Salutation (Greeting)
- It is the opening greeting of the letter.
- Examples: Dear Mr. Smith, / Dear Friend,

4. Body of the Letter
- It contains the core message of the letter and is generally divided into three sections:

• Opening: Purpose of writing.
• Main Content: Explanation and details.
• Closing: Expected action or final thoughts.

5. Complimentary Close
- It is the polite sign-off used at the end of the letter.
- Examples: Sincerely, Yours faithfully, Best regards, etc.

6. Signature & Typed Name
- It includes the sender's handwritten signature followed by their full printed name and designation, if applicable.

Parts of a Paragraph: 

A standard academic or structured paragraph consists of 3 main parts:

1. Topic Sentence
- It is the opening sentence of a paragraph.
- It introduces the main idea or central theme of the paragraph.

2. Supporting Sentences (Body)

- It summarizes the main point or restates the topic sentence in different words.

বাক্যটিতে “if the bus has arrived yet” অংশটি verb tell-এর সঙ্গে যুক্ত হয়ে কী জানতে চাওয়া হচ্ছে—তা প্রকাশ করছে।

প্রশ্ন করা যায়—
Can you tell me what?
→ if the bus has arrived yet
অর্থাৎ, clause-টি একটি object-এর কাজ করছে। তাই এটি Noun Clause.

• Noun clause:
- যে সব subordinate- clause noun এর কাজ করে থাকে অর্থাৎ, subject, object, compliment, বা case in apposition- এর কাজ করে থাকে তাদেরকে বলে noun clause.
- Noun clauses are used when a single word isn't enough.

• একটি বাক্যের যেসব স্থানে Noun clause  বসতে পারে -

1. Verb এর subject হিসেবে। 
Example: That he has much money is known to all.

2. Verb এর object হিসেবে।
Example: I know that he has done it.

3. Verb এর complement হিসেবে।
Example: This is what I said.

4. Preposition এর object হিসেবে;
Example: I cannot understand the meaning of what he said.

5. Noun/ pronoun - এর apposition হিসেবে।
Example: The fact that he is a thief is clear to all.

- Advanced Learner's Grammar and Composition by Chowdhury and Hossain.

স্পেশাল বিসিএস [স্বাস্থ্য] - সাধারণ অংশ.exp:
She could not attend the meeting because she was busy. Here, 'because she was busy' is - Adverbial clause of reason.
বাক্যটিতে “because she was busy” অংশটি She could not attend the meeting- এই ঘটনার কারণ প্রকাশ করছে।

প্রশ্ন করা যায়—
Why could she not attend the meeting?
→ Because she was busy.

অর্থাৎ, clause-টি কেন সে meeting-এ উপস্থিত হতে পারেনি, তার reason বা cause নির্দেশ করছে। তাই এটি Adverbial Clause of Reason.

• Adverbial clause of reason:
- Because, as, since-প্রভৃতি দ্বারা কোন clause শুরু হলে তা 'কারণ' নির্দেশ করে। এরূপ clause-কে বলে adverbial clause of reason. যেমনঃ
- Example: He could not go to school because he was ill.
- (সে স্কুলে যেতে পারেনি কারণ সে ছিল অসুস্থ।)

• Other options:
• Adverbial clause of condition
- If, unless, in case, whether, on condition that, provided (that), supposing (that)-ইত্যাদি দ্বারা কোনো clause আরম্ভ হলে তা কোনো "শর্ত” প্রকাশ করে। এই জাতীয় clause কে বলে adverbial clause of condition বা conditional clause.
- Example: If you come, I shall go.
- (যদি তুমি আস তাহলে আমি যাব।)
- এখানে if = যদি। If you come-দ্বারা একটি শর্ত বুঝানো হচ্ছে। এই শর্ত পালিত না হলে আমি যাব না-ভাবটা এরকম।

• Adverbial Clauses of Manner:
- এ Clause দ্বারা Principal Clause এর কার্য কীভাবে সম্পন্ন হয় তা নির্দেশ করে।
- এ Clause সাধারণত: as, like, how, however ইত্যাদি দ্বারা শুরু হয়।
- অধিকাংশ ক্ষেত্রে উপরোক্ত Subordinating Conjunction গুলো principal clause এর পরে বসে।
- Example: You can travel however you like.

• Adverbial clause of Time:
- While, whenever, when ইত্যাদি দিয়ে যে সব adverb clause শুরু হয় তারা কোনো সময় বা মুহূর্তকে নির্দেশ করে। এদেরকে বলে Adverbial clause of time.
- We shall start when he comes. (যখন সে আসে তখন আমরা শুরু করব।)
- She will dance whenever her sister comes. (যখনই তার বোন আসবে তখনই সে নাচবে।)

Source: A Passage to the English Language, S. M. Zakir Hussain.

Parts of a Paragraph: 

A standard academic or structured paragraph consists of 3 main parts:

1. Topic Sentence
- It is the opening sentence of a paragraph.
- It introduces the main idea or central theme of the paragraph.

2. Supporting Sentences (Body)
- These sentences develop, explain, and support the main idea of the paragraph.
- They may include details, facts, examples, reasons, or explanations.

3. Concluding Sentence
- It is the final sentence of the paragraph.
- It summarizes the main point or restates the topic sentence in different words.
- It may also provide a smooth transition to the next paragraph.
